hardware.variant: One assembled kit with operator-reported CoreBoard V1.2.

inputs.name: ESP_MOSAICO_SC101IOT PP RX protocol diagnostic FIT
inputs.revision: Candidate RAM kernel based on OS baseline a88ec7252aa plus the 4e56 PP RX diagnostic; not current main net80211.

inputs.name: WPA2-PSK/CCMP/PMF0 profile and selected AP
inputs.revision: Pinned AP0 control trial; identifiers omitted.

scenario: On one operator-reported ESP-Mosaico V1.2 sample, run one bounded WPA2-PSK/CCMP/PMF0 control trial using the PP RX protocol diagnostic FIT, recording FC type and rxmatch0 counts before the ROM routing check.
expected: Reach WPA_COMPLETED while recording the ppRxProtoProc and normal STA callback boundaries, native state, opaque hardware counters, and internal-pool pressure.
observed: The station reached ASSOCIATED but not WPA_COMPLETED; the final supplicant status was ASSOCIATED and the kernel later disconnected with reason 204. Native Wi-Fi state advanced init→auth→assoc→run with RX policy 6, then run→init (0xcc00). The pp_wdev_funcs table at ppRxProtoProc +0x198 remained 0x2f030070, wrapper_match=1, with slot 1 at both begin and end. Its FC matrix (management/control/data/extension × rxmatch0 clear/set) was 0/123, 0/0, 0/0, 0/0; invalid and short counts were zero. The normal pTxRx table remained 0x80625408 with the +0x3f8 wrapper matched; sta_rx_cb ran 123 times, all management type, with control/data/extension counts 0/0/0. sta_input_table, crypto_decap, decap and sta_rx_eapol each remained zero. AP0 logs recorded association, station deauthentication after a PTK 4-way handshake timeout, another association and station disassociation; these records do not prove AP M1 transmission or station ACK. Hardware statistics getter succeeded, but rx_datasuc=123 and rx_buf_fullcnt=96 are opaque values, not frame-type evidence. Internal-pool misses, fallbacks and final NULL were zero; the window minimum free was 197136 bytes.

measurements.name: disconnect-reason
measurements.unit: local disconnect after PTK 4-way handshake timeout

measurements.name: diagnostic-window
measurements.unit: seconds from debug enable through disconnect

measurements.name: hardware-rx-datasuc
measurements.unit: opaque hardware counter; not a DATA frame count

measurements.name: hardware-rx-buffer-full
measurements.unit: opaque hardware counter; not proof of allocation failure

limits: One operator-reported V1.2 sample and one RAM-loaded candidate diagnostic kernel; this does not establish support for other revisions or persistent Wi-Fi operation.

The ppRxProtoProc wrapper is called from both ppRxPkt routing branches after dequeue and earlier vendor stages, before fragment and rxmatch0 checks. It saw no control, DATA or extension frames in this window. It is not an over-the-air or all-hardware observer, so this result does not determine whether the AP transmitted a frame or where any earlier loss occurred.
The normal STA callback also saw management frames only. Zero DATA at either measured boundary does not establish whether DATA reached unobserved hardware or ROM stages.

AP0 logs record association and station deauthentication after the PTK timeout, not AP transmission or station acknowledgement of M1. Successful-empty association snapshots can miss short associations.
Hardware rx_datasuc and rx_buf_fullcnt are opaque counters and do not identify frame type or prove memory pressure. Internal-pool misses, fallback and NULL were zero in this measured window.
No EAPOL input, WPA_COMPLETED, negotiated PMF, IP address, DNS or accepted network data exchange was observed. Wi-Fi support remains partial.
